definitions.explanation: A wide, expansive view seen from a high or distant vantage point. Emphasizes the act of gazing out over a landscape and the scenery itself.

examples.japanese: {眺望|ちょうぼう}がすばらしい。
この{部屋|へや}からは{海|うみ}の{眺望|ちょうぼう}が{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: You can enjoy an ocean view from this room.

examples.japanese: {山頂|さんちょう}からの{眺望|ちょうぼう}は{息|いき}を{呑|の}むほど{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The panoramic view from the mountaintop was breathtakingly beautiful.

notes:
A somewhat formal or literary word for a panoramic view from an elevated or distant vantage point. Composed of {眺|なが}める (to gaze) + {望|のぞ}む (to look out over), both characters conveying the sense of looking far into the distance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {眺望|ちょうぼう}がいい: to have a good view
- {眺望|ちょうぼう}を{楽|たの}しむ: to enjoy the view
- {眺望|ちょうぼう}が{開|ひら}ける: the view opens up
- {眺望|ちょうぼう}を{遮|さえぎ}る: to block the view
- {眺望|ちょうぼう}スポット: viewpoint, scenic lookout

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {景色|けしき}: scenery — the most common everyday word for natural scenery
- {風景|ふうけい}: landscape — slightly more literary; used for broader scenic views
- {展望|てんぼう}: outlook, prospect — often used for observation decks ({展望台|てんぼうだい}) and figuratively for future prospects
- {眺|なが}め: view — more casual and conversational than {眺望|ちょうぼう}

USAGE:
Frequently used in real estate listings, travel writing, and hotel descriptions to highlight scenic views. More formal than {眺|なが}め and emphasizes grandeur.
